feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and relevance: web, CMS, analytics, email, social, video, governance, and strategy are all well aligned to digital communications leadership roles.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to scan, with no major spelling errors or obvious typos.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (growth %, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, revenue/supporter impact, adoption metrics).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); consider consistent capitalization of terms like “organization-wide” and date formatting (“Sept.”/“Oct.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a more distinctive leadership angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Reduce the long channel list unless needed for the role; it duplicates later skills sections.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple work experience bullets and could be shortened in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, senior-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Reduce overlap with softer competencies by removing “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” which is already covered in the header and Soft Skills.
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use mostly noun phrases and avoid mixing broad functions with tactical outputs.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Multi-channel communications leadership • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Content systems architecture • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already used in the header.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and weakens this section’s technical/strategic focus.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and what is new at consultant level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like Led, Built, Launched, Advised, Improved.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams supported.
- Rephrase for specificity: “Built Drupal microsites and modular campaign components” is stronger than “develop campaign and storytelling experiences”; “designed retrieval strategy and structured content workflows for AI search” is stronger than “lead development.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats footer project details (AI search, microsite, anniversary campaign); keep the role high-level and let projects hold examples.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting scope, embedded leadership, and new AI/search work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in engagement, production savings from the in-house studio, reporting efficiency gains, or governance improvements (e.g., faster publishing, fewer errors, better cross-team adoption).
- Combine lower-value bullets for concision: merge analytics + governance into one operational-improvement bullet if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; here, emphasize building the studio and scaling institutional capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: editorial operations, newsletter execution, and establishing repeatable advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function, not “helping”: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show creation/scale: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets and add outcomes if available: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.” Add metrics if possible (send volume, video cadence, turnaround time, engagement).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” repeats the Director role; emphasize execution/coordination here, strategy/governance there.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this version as scaling/formalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level wording tied to current work:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization  
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)  
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Cut “Audience-focused content planning”; it reads junior/generic compared with the rest of the CV.
- Consider “content operations” over “content leadership” to better match the systems/governance emphasis in recent roles.
- If space allows, add one qualifier such as “for high-volume public-sector organizations” to reinforce specialization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already well evidenced in the NACo Director role; avoid repeating it elsewhere without a sharper angle.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, higher-value capabilities: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent strengths first: put Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow integration, and AI-enabled search ahead of older/general platforms.
- Consider dropping weaker or less central platforms here (e.g., SharePoint, Power Pages, WordPress) unless they are target-role keywords; keep those in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Search and workflow automation” rather than generic nouns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; use Topline Skills for strategic/marketable themes, not exhaustive platform inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business-facing wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics/reporting language unless clarified as “SEO, UX and site performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make it feel more senior and outcomes-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ and multi-camera studio systems,” “Virtual event operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio operations • Virtual event production”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to impact from recent roles: in-house studio buildout, recurring advocacy programming, event support.
- Drop “editing” unless paired with a stronger term like “end-to-end production”; “studio operations” alone is vague.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level detail here overlaps with “Premiere Pro,” “Audition,” and “Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent work, lead with it and add light context or proficiency signals.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding a qualifier to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just tools: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it reflects meaningful use; otherwise replace with a stronger enterprise platform or remove for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Topline Skills – Web Platforms & Technical Execution” entry almost exactly; differentiate this section as platform-specific only.
- Avoid repeating Drupal context elsewhere unless tied to a distinct achievement.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools tied to recent delivery work and clarifying level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more execution-oriented, e.g. **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**.
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**.
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent projects; if kept, place it last or label it **legacy support**.
- If space allows, add specificity that signals applied use: **front-end implementation, lightweight scripting, deployment automation, edge/serverless functions**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** plus **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- **Workflow automation** in Topline Skills may also overlap with **GitHub Actions**; keep one high-level, one tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “Used to support cross-team planning, content operations, and process automation.”
- Consider dropping the weakest/oldest-use tools if not current; keep the list focused on platforms most relevant to recent consulting and director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less differentiation than Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier/Jira.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused without repeating channel management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability layer instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation**
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it rather than padding the list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands of recipients,” or engagement outcomes here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-stage buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer execution scope: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this role as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” and “digital team” echo later leadership roles; keep this item focused on setup and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize project coordination plus the standout launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support verb: “produced” or “developed multimedia content/materials.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; one concise sentence or two compact bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating generic web/email/social language here unless this role directly owned those channels.
